# agent-do

> Provider-agnostic autonomous agent loop for JavaScript. Built on the Vercel AI SDK.

## Core

- `createAgent(config: AgentConfig): Agent` — create an agent with run(), stream(), abort()
- `runAgentLoop(config, task, context?, history?): Promise<RunResult>` — run loop directly
- `streamAgentLoop(config, task, context?, history?): AsyncGenerator<ProgressEvent>` — stream events

## Agent Interface

- `agent.run(task, context?, history?): Promise<string>` — synchronous execution
- `agent.stream(task, context?, history?): AsyncIterable<ProgressEvent>` — streaming execution
- `agent.abort()` — cancel the current run
- `agent.id: string` — agent identifier
- `agent.name: string` — agent display name

## ProgressEvent Types

- `thinking` — model is generating
- `tool-call` — calling a tool (toolName, toolArgs)
- `tool-result` — tool returned (toolName, toolResult)
- `text` — text output
- `step-complete` — loop iteration finished
- `done` — agent completed
- `error` — error or limit exceeded

## Tool factories

- `createMemoryTools(store: MemoryStore, agentId: string): ToolSet` — agent's private scratchpad (memory_read/write/list/delete/search). Pass any MemoryStore.
- `createWorkspaceTools(workingDir: string, opts?): ToolSet` — project files (read_file/write_file/edit_file/list_directory/delete_file/grep_file/find_files) rooted at workingDir, with a sensible deny-list (.env/.ssh/**/...). `opts.sandbox?: SandboxApi` swaps the internal store for SandboxBackedMemoryStore.
- `createShellTool(sandbox: SandboxApi, opts?): ToolSet` — single shell tool (default model name `bash`) wired to a SandboxApi. The sandbox is required: pass an isolating connector, or `createHostSandbox()` explicitly for host execution (not isolation). Output is returned inside `<tool_output>` markers with injection-marker redaction.

## Memory Stores

- `InMemoryMemoryStore` — in-memory (testing/prototyping, data lost on exit)
- `FilesystemMemoryStore(baseDir: string, options?: FilesystemMemoryStoreOptions)` — Node.js filesystem (persistent)
  - `options.readOnly: boolean` — block all write operations
  - `options.onBeforeWrite: (agentId, canonicalPath, operation) => boolean | Promise<boolean>` — approve/deny each write
- `SandboxBackedMemoryStore(sandbox: SandboxApi, root?: string, options?)` — adapt any sandbox connector into a MemoryStore. Mirrors readOnly / onBeforeWrite from FilesystemMemoryStore.
- `MemoryStore` interface: read, write, append, delete, list, mkdir, exists, search

## Sandbox (#3)

- Sandboxing is **per-provider** — there is no `AgentConfig.sandbox` field. Each store/tool decides whether to route through one.
- `SandboxApi` contract (Flue spec): readFile, readFileBuffer, writeFile, stat, readdir, exists, mkdir, rm, exec
- Connectors:
  - `createHostSandbox(opts?)` — direct host passthrough; **not a security boundary**. `exec()` builds a fail-closed environment instead of inheriting the parent's: `PATH`, `HOME`, `LANG`, `LANGUAGE`, `LC_*`, `TMPDIR`, `TZ`, `TERM`, `SHELL`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `NODE_ENV`, plus the Windows platform set (`SystemRoot`, `COMSPEC`, `APPDATA`, `TEMP`, …) only on Windows. `opts.envPassthrough: string[]` forwards extra **exact** names (never patterns); `opts.inheritEnv: true` forwards the whole parent environment (pre-0.8 behaviour — only for commands that genuinely need it); `opts.cwd` sets the default working directory. `ExecOptions.env` is caller-supplied library code and wins over all three.
  - `createJustBashSandbox(opts?)` / `wrapJustBashSandbox(instance)` — vercel-labs/just-bash virtual fs + bash interpreter (optional peer dep)
- How to route through a sandbox:
  - Memory: `createMemoryTools(new SandboxBackedMemoryStore(sandbox, '/memory'), agentId)`
  - Workspace: `createWorkspaceTools(dir, { sandbox })`
  - Shell: `createShellTool(sandbox)`
- Network policy is per-connector (allowNet), not on the contract
- A `MemoryStore` only needs to go through the sandbox when its substrate is the host filesystem. In-memory / S3 / Firestore stores have their own substrate and don't need the sandbox.

## Skills

- `InMemorySkillStore` — in-memory skill storage
- `parseSkillMd(content: string): Skill` — parse SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter
- `buildSkillsPrompt(skills: Skill[]): string` — build system prompt section
- `createSkillTools(store: SkillStore): ToolSet` — search/install/list/remove skills

## Policies

- `createPolicy({ id, type, content } | { id, type, source }): Policy` — build a typed policy (object or POLICY.md source)
- `parsePolicyMd(content, id?): Policy` — parse a policy doc with YAML frontmatter
- `buildPoliciesPrompt(policies: Policy[]): string` — build the `## Policies` system-prompt section
- `InMemoryPolicyStore` — in-memory policy storage (install/list/get/remove)

## Orchestration

- `createOrchestrator(config: OrchestratorConfig): Orchestrator` — master + workers
- Master gets: delegate_task, list_agents, get_agent_status tools
- `orchestrator.run(task)` / `orchestrator.stream(task)`

## Slash Commands (#76)

- `AgentConfig.slashCommands?: Record<string, Agent>` — deterministic pre-model dispatch keyed on the first token
- `/<name> <rest>` routes to the sub-agent with `rest`; unknown `/<name>` returns a listing (no model call); non-slash input bypasses the router
- Sub-agents are full Agent instances (own model/tools/skills); nested `/a/b` is rejected at `createAgent()` time
- Parent history is NOT forwarded by default
- `parseSlashCommand(input): { name, rest } | null` — inspect routing yourself
- `unknownSlashCommandMessage(name, commands): string` — build the listing
- `validateSlashCommands(commands): string | null` — validate a map

## Routines (#77)

- `AgentConfig.routines?: Routine[] | RoutineStore` — named prompt-as-macro procedures the model can invoke
- `parseRoutineMd(content, id?): Routine` — parse a ROUTINE.md with YAML frontmatter
- `interpolateRoutine(routine, inputs): string` — fill `{{input}}` placeholders
- `createRoutineTools(store): ToolSet` — list/run routine tools
- `InMemoryRoutineStore` / `FilesystemRoutineStore(dir)` — storage backends
- Types: `Routine`, `RoutineStore`, `RoutineInput`, `CreateRoutineToolsOptions`

## MCP (Model Context Protocol)

- `mountMcpServers(servers: McpServerConfig[]): Promise<MountedMcpServers>` — connect external MCP tool servers and return their tools plus a `close()`
- `namespacedToolName(server, tool): string` / `MCP_TOOL_PREFIX` — tools are namespaced so they can't collide with workspace or memory tools
- `McpTransportConfig` — stdio or HTTP/SSE transport
- Always `close()` mounted servers when the run ends; they own child processes or sockets

## Scheduled Tasks (#79)

- Declarative cron-driven agent runs with lock-file concurrency control
- `matchesCron(expr, date): boolean` — 5-field cron matcher
- `validateScheduledTasks(config): string | null` — validate a config before running
- `runScheduledTask(task, options): Promise<...>` — execute one task under a lock
- `readStatus(dir)` / `writeStatus(dir, status)` / `recordRun(...)` — durable run status
- Types: `ScheduledTask`, `ScheduledTasksConfig`, `TaskStatus`, `StatusRecord`
- CLI: `npx agent-do scheduled-tasks <run|list|status|install|start>`

## Structured Tool Results (#48)

- `ToolResult` — `{ summary, data?, ... }`; tools may return one instead of a bare string
- `normaliseToolResult(value): ToolResult` — coerce any tool return into the structured shape
- `isToolResult(value): boolean` — type guard
- `tool-result` ProgressEvents carry `summary` and `data` when the tool returned a ToolResult

## File Locking (#15 Tier 1)

- Opt-in cross-process safety for `FilesystemMemoryStore`; off by default
- `acquireFileLock(path, options?): Promise<LockHandle>` — acquire, caller releases
- `withFileLock(path, fn, options?)` — acquire / run / release
- Types: `FileLockOptions`, `LockHandle`, `LockAdapter` (bring your own backend)
- Enable per-store via `FilesystemMemoryStoreOptions.lock`

## Debugging & Observability (#72)

- `AgentConfig.debug?: DebugConfig` — structured `DebugEvent`s for requests, messages, cache metrics, and raw stream parts
- CLI equivalent: `--log-level silent|info|verbose|debug|trace` (`--verbose` implies `verbose`)

## Lifecycle Hooks

- `onPreToolUse(event)` — before tool call, return HookDecision to allow/deny/modify
- `onPostToolUse(event)` — after tool call, with duration
- `onStepStart(event)` — before each iteration, return stop to halt
- `onStepComplete(event)` — after each iteration
- `onComplete(event)` — when run finishes, with full usage
- `onUsage(record)` — after each LLM call with token counts

## Permissions

- `mode: 'accept-all' | 'deny-all' | 'ask'`
- Per-tool overrides: `tools: { read_file: 'always', delete_file: 'never' }`
- `onPermissionRequest(toolName, args): Promise<boolean>`

## Usage Tracking

- `UsageTracker` — tracks tokens and cost per run
- `estimateCost(model, inputTokens, outputTokens, pricing?): number`
- `DEFAULT_PRICING: PricingTable` — built-in per-1M-token rates for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Mistral, Groq, Perplexity, Z.ai/GLM, and local models
- Model IDs are matched exactly first, then by **longest** matching prefix, so dated variants (`gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`) resolve to the most specific entry
- An unpriced model estimates `0` and logs a one-time stderr warning — cost tracking and spending limits are disabled for it. Override with `AgentConfig.usage.pricing`.
- `resetPricingWarnings()` — clear the warned-model set (tests / long-lived servers)
- Per-run and per-day spending limits

## Testing

- `createMockModel(options: MockModelOptions)` ��� mock LanguageModel with predetermined responses
- Import from `agent-do/testing`

## ConversationMessage

- `{ role: 'user' | 'assistant', content: string }` — for passing conversation history

## Prompt Builder (agent-do/prompts)

- `buildSystemPrompt(options: BuildSystemPromptOptions): string` — compose a system prompt
  - `options.template: string | PromptTemplate` — named template or custom template object
  - `options.sectionOrder: string[]` — override section order
  - `options.sections: Record<string, SectionFn>` — custom/override section functions
  - `options.variables: Record<string, string>` — interpolated into sections
  - `options.append: Array<string | SectionFn>` — content appended after sections
  - `options.prepend: Array<string | SectionFn>` — content prepended before sections
- `interpolate(template, variables): string` — {{variable}} replacement
- `builtinTemplates` — assistant, coder, researcher, reviewer, writer, planner
- `builtinSections` — identity, memoryManagement, fileTools, efficiency, concise, selfEditing, learnedPreferences, htmlGeneration, todoTracking, runtimeContext
- `roleSections` — codingApproach, researchApproach, reviewApproach, writingApproach, planningApproach

## Eval Framework (agent-do/eval)

- `defineEval(config: EvalSuiteConfig): EvalSuiteConfig` — define an eval suite
- `runEvals(suite, options?): Promise<EvalResult>` — run evals, return structured results
- `evaluateAssertion(assertion, result, judgeModel?): Promise<AssertionResult>` — evaluate one assertion
- Assertion types: contains, not-contains, regex, json-schema, tool-called, tool-not-called, tool-args, file-exists, file-contains, max-steps, max-cost, llm-rubric, custom
- Output formats: console (default), json, csv, silent
- Multi-provider comparison via `options.providers: Array<{ name, model }>`
- LLM-as-judge via `llm-rubric` assertion with configurable score type (pass-fail or 1-5)
- Custom assertions via `{ type: 'custom', name, fn: (result) => boolean }`
- Each case gets isolated memory store — no state leaks between cases
- `options.concurrency: number` — parallel case execution (default: 1)

## CLI (npx agent-do)

- Fresh prompt sessions include lazy, anonymous Parallel Search MCP tools `mcp__parallel__web_search` and `mcp__parallel__web_fetch`. Approve interactively or with `--allow`; tool calls have a 30-second deadline and respect cancellation.
- `--no-search` or `--no-tools` disables the default web tools. Explicit `--provider-tool` / `--provider-options` suppresses this default; saved agents, scripts, evals and library configurations are unchanged.
- `npx agent-do "prompt"` — one-shot task with default agent
- `npx agent-do` — interactive chat REPL
- `echo "context" | npx agent-do "prompt"` — pipe stdin as context, merged with prompt
- `npx agent-do create <name>` — create a saved agent config (.agent-do/agents/<name>.json)
- `npx agent-do list` — list saved agents
- `npx agent-do run <name|file>` — run a saved agent by name, or a script file
- `npx agent-do eval <file|dir>` — run eval cases from file or directory
- `npx agent-do scheduled-tasks <run|list|status|install|start>` — cron-driven runs (#79)
- `npx agent-do <file.shellm>` — prompt files as executable scripts (#16)
- `--provider <name>` — anthropic | google | openai | ollama | zai (default: anthropic)
- `--model <id>` — model ID. Per-provider defaults: anthropic `claude-sonnet-5`, google `gemini-3.6-flash`, openai `gpt-5.6-terra`, ollama `llama3.2`, zai `glm-4.6`.
- `--system <prompt>` — system prompt
- `--memory <dir>` — memory directory (default: .agent-do/)
- `--read-only` — no filesystem writes
- `--verbose` — show tool calls
- `--json` — JSON output
- `--compare <providers>` — eval: compare across providers (comma-separated)
- `--output <format>` — eval: console | json | csv
- `--concurrency <n>` — eval: parallel case execution
- `--provider-tool <name>` — enable a provider-native tool (repeatable). Names resolve against the installed `<provider>.tools` surface; aliases like `webSearch` map to the latest dated export. Examples: `googleSearch`, `urlContext`, `codeExecution`, `webSearch`, `bash`, `fileSearch`.
- `--provider-options <json>` — provider-specific options forwarded to every model call (e.g. `'{"google":{"useSearchGrounding":true}}'`). Persisted on saved agents created with the same flag.

## AgentConfig provider options

- `AgentConfig.providerOptions?: ProviderOptions` — `Record<string, Record<string, JSONValue>>`. Forwarded verbatim to every `streamText` call. Use for Google `useSearchGrounding`, Anthropic `thinking`, OpenAI `reasoningEffort`, etc. Anthropic prompt-cache control is set per-message and survives this merge.
- Provider-native *tools* go in `AgentConfig.tools` as the SDK's tool factories produce them — `tools: { google_search: google.tools.googleSearch({}) }`.
